messages:
anna: ran a focused perf sweep for quant-llm-11b (int8 bring-up) across same-sku A100s on AWS/GCP/Azure. GCP (us-central1) is showing higher throughput and tighter p99s than the others.

rajesh: paste the exact run config + how you measured

anna: config:
```
model: quant-llm-11b-int8
batch_size: 8
seq_len: 2048
warmup: 50
measure: 200
image: redwood/llm-infer:canary-2026-03
runner: perf-runner v0.9
metrics: tokens/s, p50, p95, p99
```
Single GPU, pinned, no interleaving, 3 repeats per region.

perf-bot: job/1851234567-sweep started on aws/us-west-2, gcp/us-central1, azure/eastus

sophie: what driver/cuda versions on each host? that tends to matter

anna: aws/us-west-2 -> NVIDIA 525.85 + CUDA 11.8
gcp/us-central1 -> NVIDIA 535.54 + CUDA 12.1
azure/eastus -> NVIDIA 525.60 + CUDA 11.8
(so only GCP is on driver535/CUDA12)

deniz: CUDA12/driver535 can switch to newer cuBLAS/cuBLASLt heuristics. check CUBLAS_LOG_INFO and CUPTI to see which kernels are selected

anna: quick numbers (median of repeats):
- GCP (CUDA12): 760 tok/s, p99 65 ms
- AWS (CUDA11.8): 695 tok/s, p99 98 ms
- Azure (CUDA11.8): 702 tok/s, p99 92 ms

carlos: ~9-10% throughput delta and ~30ms p99 gap. that's significant. did you capture kernel timelines?

anna: rerunning with tracing. command:
```
export CUBLAS_LOG_INFO=1
export CUPTI_ACTIVITY_KIND=CONCURRENT_KERNEL,CONTEXT
perf-runner --trace=cupti --out=./traces/${region}.tgz
```
Uploading when done.

sophie: next step: driver parity test. install driver535/CUDA12 on an AWS host (or mount CUDA12 libs in docker) and rerun. if gap closes => algorithm/heuristics. if not => hw microcode/firmware differences.

anna: spinning up AWS nodes with driver535 now. also toggling TF32 (CUBLAS_ALLOW_TENSOR_OP_MATH) and trying to force cublasLt/off. early note: disabling TF32 drops GCP throughput ~20% (expected), but switching TF32 doesn't fully explain AWS/GCP gap.

deniz: also capture cublasLt vs cublas API calls — newer TF32 paths may go through cuBLASLt with different tiling. CUPTI traces should show cuBLASLt kernels if used.

carlos: do a small batch sweep (batch 1..16) and a short seq_len sweep (512/1024/2048) to see where divergence starts (startup vs steady-state).

anna: will run those. filing infra ticket to repro driver parity across clouds and opening vendor support with cuBLAS logs if necessary.

rajesh: great. ping when traces are uploaded and when driver-parity run completes. will assign someone to follow up on vendor side if gap persists.

perf-bot: uploads:
- gs://redwood-perf/traces/1851234567-gcp.tgz
- s3://redwood-perf/traces/1851234567-aws.tgz
- https://azure.blob/redwood/1851234567-azure.tgz

sophie: nice, thanks anna. next step: AWS with CUDA12 tomorrow :thumbsup:

anna: will report back with the parity results and kernel timelines. closing this thread until we have the driver-parity runs.
